clue.text: Took seat in Birnam maybe, proving likely cabinet material?

parts.note: to take a seat is to sit, so 'took seat' gives the past tense sat
taken as written
Birnam Wood, which comes to Dunsinane in Macbeth, is an example of a wood

explanation.surface: Someone sits down in a Scottish forest that turns out to be good timber for furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birnam' looks like a place to sit, but it stands for the wood of Macbeth fame, with 'maybe' marking it as one example of a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinwood is a lustrous yellowish timber prized by furniture makers for veneered cabinets.

clue.text: Fight's hottest in the centre, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the central letters are read in reverse order
the letters in the centre of the word hottest are taken, dropping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A brawl is at its fiercest in the middle, so someone reflects on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the centre' leaves OTTES from hottest, and 'on reflection' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief, heated quarrel or scrap, so it is a kind of fight.

clue.text: Local authorities with time to admit everyone into High School

parts.note: to own up to something is to admit it

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes into the abbreviation for High School

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Councils let all comers into the local secondary school, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts ALL inside HS to make HALLS, after T and OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Town halls are the seats of local councils, so the buildings stand by metonymy for the councils themselves.

clue.text: Nook, rather out-of-the-way, in exotic land

indicators.note: read as 'out of the usual way', it tells the solver to put the letters of the two words in a new order

explanation.surface: A remote corner tucked away in some foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out-of-the-way' looks like a description of the nook, but it is the signal to rearrange NOOK and RATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korea is an isolated Asian state, strange and distant to most readers, hence an exotic land.

clue.text: Applied decoration excessively — not professional

parts.note: over as a prefix means too much, as in overdone
lay means not belonging to a profession, as in a layman

explanation.surface: An amateur decorator has piled on the ornament far too thickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlay is a thin layer of ornament laid onto a surface, such as gold leaf or veneer.

clue.text: File rough sleeper, gripping point of implement

indicators.note: holding something tightly means it sits inside, so the sleeper's word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a dosser is someone who sleeps rough, a British slang word for a homeless person

indicators.note: the point or tip of the word implement is its first letter

explanation.surface: A homeless person grabs the sharp end of a tool, perhaps a rasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'File' looks like the tool, matching 'implement', but it means a set of papers. 'gripping' puts I, from 'point of', inside DOSSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of papers about one subject, the same as a file.

clue.text: Game found in very Etonian setting, primarily

indicators.note: primarily, read as 'in the first place', asks for the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A sport played in a very Etonian environment, chiefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: fives, a handball game played in a walled court, is strongly associated with Eton College, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Fives is a court game in which a ball is struck with the gloved hand.

clue.text: Something that happens in first part of Farquhar play

indicators.note: the first part of the name Farquhar is its opening letter

parts.note: to act is to play a role on stage

explanation.surface: An event takes place in the opening section of a Farquhar drama.
explanation.walkthrough: George Farquhar was an Irish Restoration playwright, which makes 'play' read as a noun; it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is an event or circumstance that really occurred, a thing that happens.

clue.text: Delivery vehicle heading for Dover carries one exotic type of food

indicators.note: the vehicle and letter carry the next piece inside them

parts.note: a van is a vehicle used for deliveries
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the heading of Dover is the letter at its head, its first

explanation.surface: A van bound for Dover is carrying some foreign foodstuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts I inside VAN plus D, the head of Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: Viand is an old literary word for an article of food, unusual enough to sound foreign.

clue.text: Oversupplied with fruit seed for replanting

indicators.note: replanting puts the seeds in fresh positions, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener has too much fruit seed to sow again.
explanation.definitionFit: Surfeited means given too much of something, glutted.

clue.text: Vehicle breakdown specialist given rise

explanation.surface: A recovery mechanic is promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tow-er is someone who tows broken-down cars away; to tower is to rise high above.

clue.text: Furnishing midshipman with academic appointment

parts.note: Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel
a chair is a professorship at a university

explanation.surface: Providing a junior naval officer with a university professorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furnishing' looks like a verb, providing, but it is a noun, an item of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large comfortable armchair, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Cook initially hungry chimp a lot of mince pies?

indicators.note: to cook is to mix up ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order
initially means the first letter of the word hungry

explanation.surface: A ravenous ape is told to bake a great many mince pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges H (the first of 'hungry') with CHIMP, A and LOT. 'Mince pies' is Cockney rhyming slang for eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophthalmic means relating to the eyes, which rhyming slang calls mince pies.

clue.text: Golf club discounting women's keenness

indicators.note: discounting a thing leaves it out, so the letter is removed from the club

parts.note: a wedge is a golf club with a steeply angled face
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: A golf club that leaves out the women's section.
explanation.definitionFit: Edge means sharpness or eagerness, as in an edge to one's appetite.

clue.text: See woman as recipient of attack, one that's unthinking

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, in references

indicators.note: the woman receives the next pieces, holding them inside her name

parts.note: Eve is the first woman of Genesis
to get at someone is to attack or criticise them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Look: a woman on the receiving end of an assault from a mindless lout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as recipient of' puts GETAT and I inside EVE, all after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetative describes a state of bare existence without thought, like a plant's.

clue.text: Use cunning to cover depression, appearing slender and graceful

indicators.note: the word for cunning is put over the other, covering it by surrounding it

parts.note: wily means cunning or crafty
a low is an area of low pressure, a weather depression

explanation.surface: Advice to hide a slump in spirits by being crafty and looking lithe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' simply tells the solver to employ the cunning word. 'to cover' puts LOW inside WILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Willowy describes a tall, lithe figure, slim and supple as a willow.

clue.text: Philosophy uniquely available to astronauts?

explanation.surface: Space travellers alone may hold a certain outlook on life.
explanation.definitionFit: A world view is an overall philosophy of life; read literally it is a sight of the whole planet, which only those in space get.

clue.text: Put in again (but not at Lord's, we hear?)

definitions.text: Put in again (but not at Lord's, we hear?)

parts.words: Put in again (but not at Lord's, we hear?)
parts.note: putting someone into office once more by votes, unlike the House of Lords whose members are not chosen at the polls; at Lord's cricket ground 'put in' would mean sent in to bat

explanation.surface: Restore someone to office, though not in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, where a side 'put in' is made to bat; the clue warns against that sense and the unelected House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elect is to vote someone into an office again.

clue.text: Came up with a diet designed to make you very thin

indicators.note: designed means put together to a new plan, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somebody invented a slimming plan meant to make you skeletal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges CAME and A DIET; 'up with' and 'to make you' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin from lack of food.

clue.text: Point to consider

explanation.surface: A detail worth weighing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A respect is a particular point or detail, as in 'in every respect'; to respect is also to regard or take into account.

clue.text: People in authority accepting charge for treatment

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the people's word contains the charge

parts.note: 'they' is the everyday name for the unnamed powers that be
a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap

explanation.surface: Officials take on a fee for medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee, but it is a criminal charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment meant to heal or relieve an illness or disorder.

clue.text: It's official, of course

parts.note: read as an official at a racecourse or golf course rather than 'naturally it is formal'

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but it means attached to a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an official who oversees a race meeting and enforces its rules.

clue.text: Eyes shut, maybe, after end of tedious French article

indicators.note: the end of the word tedious is its last letter

parts.note: le is a French word for 'the'

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of the word shut are only one possible arrangement, so reorder them

explanation.surface: Eyes closing, perhaps, after the end of a boring French piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyes' are private eyes; 'after' puts UTHS (SHUT rearranged by 'maybe') after S and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Private eyes are detectives, and so are sleuths.

clue.text: Game in diamonds?

explanation.surface: A sport played among jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Dice is a game of chance; to dice is to mark or cut in a chequered pattern of squares, which set on point look like diamonds.

clue.text: One implicated in credit note fraud, possibly

indicators.note: being implicated in something means being caught inside it, so the letter goes within the others

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
me is a form of mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone involved in a dodgy credit note scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'implicated in' puts I inside CR and ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is one example of an offence against the law.

clue.text: Unusually elegant do one's mounted in embassy

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters are set out differently

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A remarkably smart party is staged in a foreign mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges ELEGANT, DO and I; 'mounted in' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegation is a body of representatives sent abroad, much like an embassy.

clue.text: Politician ultimately getting very agitated and anxious

indicators.note: ultimately, read as 'at the last', asks for the final letter of politician
agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician eventually becomes very worked up and nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervy means jumpy or apprehensive.

clue.text: Here's his wife

parts.note: a goddess's name followed by 'is his wife': the husband of the queen of the Olympian gods

explanation.surface: Introducing a man's spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera, queen of Olympus, was married to the chief of the Greek gods.

clue.text: One who travels by air intent on flying

indicators.note: flying here means sent scattering, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A passenger going by plane is keen to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges AIR and INTENT; 'by' and 'on' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant is someone who travels from place to place.

clue.text: Plant, wintergreen, requiring judicious pruning

indicators.note: pruning the word wintergreen judiciously cuts letters off both ends, leaving letters from inside it

explanation.surface: A wintergreen bush needs careful cutting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like the shrub, but it is a verb: to plant a body is to bury it.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, putting in the ground as one plants.

clue.text: Daughter's after little black dresses

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
D is the abbreviation for daughter, and the plural daughters gives DS

explanation.surface: A girl is after some little black dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little black dresses' looks like one phrase, but 'little' is wordplay. 'after' puts DS after WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Widow's weeds are the black mourning clothes worn by a widow.

clue.text: Dry eyes at function on Thursday?

indicators.note: in mathematics a function maps things onto new values, so these letters are mapped into a new order

explanation.surface: Tearless at a ceremony held on a Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' rearranges DRY EYES AT; read on a Friday, Thursday is the day before.
explanation.definitionFit: Thursday is the day before if today is Friday, which is what the question mark allows.
